children: SpaceX this weekend executed a safer, more orderly landing of one of its rockets — a major milestone toward making space travel more economical and accessible. The feat was widely celebrated by Wall Street analysts.

The Elon Musk-led company caught its Starship rocket's upper stage spacecraft, from orbit on Saturday, using chopstick-like mechanical arms attached to a launch tower at its Texas facility. The catch marks a big step toward creating fully reusable rocket systems, which would vastly lower the cost of space expeditions.

Historically, engineers have struggled to recover and reuse rockets due to the damage systems sustain when re-entering earth's orbit. But that may be about to change, if SpaceX's latest experiment is any indication, according to Citigroup.

"SPCX successfully conducted Starship Flight 15, which we had the opportunity to attend at Starbase, TX alongside a range of stakeholders and company representatives," Citi analyst John Godyn said Monday in a note to clients. "Not only does Flight 15 itself – the successful catch of the Starship using Mechazilla's arms – represent one of the key milestones we've flagged along a multi-year path of upside toward $900+, but we walked away from the event with greater conviction in the outlook for the company's Super Intelligence segment as well (see SPCX - Potential for $900+)."
Citi has a buy rating on SpaceX shares, and hiked its price target to $280 from $240, suggesting the stock is double from Friday's close.
Here's what else analysts are saying about SpaceX's historic catch.

"With a ship catch, SpaceX has materially de-risked the longer-term TAMs across all 3 of its segments. Our longer-term (2028+) estimates for each segment of SpaceX are highly dependent on the success of the Starship testing path, particularly its ability to ramp reuse of both stages of Starship. For many investors, longer-term opportunities such as orbital compute or lunar cannot be seriously considered until SpaceX has Starship fully reusable with line-of-sight to rapid Cadence."

"On the back of Starship Flight 15 (on 11/13-11/14), we take the opportunity to address the operational performance of the vehicle and mission. In our view, the launch provided positive proof points around driving full and rapid reusability for the Starship launch vehicle...With the recovery of the spacecraft on 11/14, we believe that the concept around Starship reusability will become somewhat de-risked given the positive proof points achieved with the vehicle recovery (and continued operational execution)."

"SpaceX caught Ship 42 with the launch tower on Friday's Starship Test Flight 15, the company's first time recovering an orbital vehicle and a huge step toward full vehicle reusability. Before returning, the ship deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The booster was lost as its boostback burn ended early on low fuel; SpaceX is investigating the root cause. The ship catch milestone comes far ahead of schedule (vs our prior 1H:27 estimate) and establishes proof of concept for full reusability."

"The mission appears to have been largely a success, with the successful catch of the second stage most critical. This is the first time SpaceX (or any other company or government) has landed the second stage of a rocket. This catch on the launch pad appeared to go exactly as planned. In addition, unlike Flight 14, the entire orbital mission was completed. All 26 Starlink satellites were placed in orbit and the target 14 orbits were completed. The heat shield appeared to be in good condition. But, we will wait for analysis by the SpaceX team before going to conclusions. If the heat shield is found to be in good condition, we may expect to see this Starship reused on the next flight, Flight 16."

"SpaceX successfully caught Starship during Flight 15 from Starbase, TX. We view the launch outcome positively for the stock, demonstrating another key milestone for Starship through de-risking the reusability case that may enable future cost reductions across Connectivity and AI. Despite the Starship success, SPCX's Super Heavy booster did explode in the gulf after diverting away from a launchpad tower catch. SPCX noted it correctly diverted a tower catch with early indications signaling a low fuel indication on re-entry. SPCX previously caught the Super Heavy booster, and we view the diversion as not a significant risk for sentiment."

"We are reminded this past weekend that in the long arc of our SpaceX thesis (Apex of Civilizational Ambition), the success of Starship ultimately transcends all else, unlocking Starmind (orbital compute) and Starworld (Moon/Mars). Starship Flight 15 achieved the first-ever tower catch of an orbital-class upper stage (on SpaceX's first attempt). Ship 42 (second/upper stage) completed a full orbital mission including deployment of 26 Starlink V3 satellites, coasting for >22 hours (or about 14 orbits), surviving reentry, and being caught by the Mechazilla arms at the pad. The mission marks a major reusability milestone for the program and we believe our Starship launch cadence assumptions for 2027-28E should be meaningfully de-risked now."

title: Analysts are awed by SpaceX's Starship catch. Here's why
